panels.title: Forget identity, retain gender
panels.subtitle: LFW · ViT-B/32 · all 30 clients unlearn · means of 3 runs
panels.finding: EFU retains 95.37% gender accuracy with 5.12% identity accuracy; retraining gives 96.86% and 4.71%.

panels.title: Class forgetting and retained utility
panels.subtitle: CIFAR-10 · ResNet-18 · forget 1 of 10 classes · means of 3 runs
panels.finding: EFU’s retained accuracy is 2.39 pp below retraining; forgotten-class accuracy is 13.06% versus 13.72%.

takeaways: Selective forgetting: lower identity accuracy while retaining gender recognition.
Utility remains close to retraining: a 1.49-point gap on LFW and 2.39 points on CIFAR-10.

locations: Table 2, PDF page 10: LFW ViT-B/32, gender (retain) and identity (forget) accuracies.
Table 1(a), PDF page 9: ResNet-18, CIFAR-10 class-wise block; all eight method rows.
Section 5.1, PDF page 9 and 10: setup, unlearning schedule and means over three independent runs.

notes: Visually checked original pages 9 and 10 using digests/scratch-privacy/2025-efu/page-009.png and page-010.png; cross-checked text and PDF SHA-256.
All plotted values are accuracy percentages. Gender/retained accuracy is higher-is-better; identity/forgotten accuracy is lower-is-better. Each chart starts at zero.

Task-level chart uses all five rows already selected in insight result 1: retrain, three unwrapped baselines and standalone EFU. Wrapper rows omitted from that source selection remain explicitly outside the chart.
Class-wise supporting table retains all eight source rows, including wrapped baselines. The retained-accuracy gap is the transparent subtraction 94.82 - 92.43 = 2.39 pp.
PGD and FedOSD wrappers also add MAS regularization, so the table is not a pure encryption-only ablation.
No standard deviation, confidence interval or zero-forgetting claim is invented. Low forgotten accuracy is a behavioral outcome, not proof of erased influence.
Source is arXiv:2508.07873v1 (11 August 2025). Runtime and communication curves are not digitized or presented as tabulated values.
